event.title: Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza, One Crew Member Dies
event.canonical_title: Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza, One Crew Member Dies
event.summary: A Maltese-flagged diesel tanker carrying approximately 7,000 tonnes of fuel capsized off the coast of Ibiza. While all 17 crew members were rescued, one later died in the hospital. Spanish authorities are now implementing a contingency plan to address potential marine pollution risks.

timeline.summary: A diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes capsized near Ibiza, leading to the death of one crew member. Authorities have activated Spain's Level 2 maritime pollution response plan, but so far, no major spill has been reported, and environmental damage is still being assessed.

event_overview.title: About Environmental Disaster
event_overview.subject: Environmental Disaster
event_overview.summary: The event is the November 26, 2026 capsizing and partial sinking of the Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre in waters north-east of Ibiza, Spain, while it was carrying diesel from Algeciras to Barcelona. All 17 crew members were rescued, but one later died; the incident prompted maritime-rescue and pollution-prevention measures because of the vessel’s cargo and its location off the Balearic Islands.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The incident occurred in the early hours of November 26, 2026, about 25 nautical miles north-east of Ibiza.

facts.label: Vessel and voyage
facts.value: The vessel was identified by the Balearic government as the Med Emre, flying the Maltese flag and sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona.

facts.label: Crew casualties
facts.value: There were 17 crew members aboard; seven were taken to Ibiza, and one of those people died after rescue.

facts.label: Cargo and environmental risk
facts.value: Authorities and Reuters reporting said the tanker may have been carrying up to 7,000 metric tonnes of diesel, creating a potential marine-pollution risk even though no major spill had been confirmed in the initial response.

facts.label: Response framework
facts.value: The Balearic Islands activated PLATERBAL at level 0; Spain’s national marine-pollution response system provides for maritime, coastal, regional and local contingency plans when pollution could affect Spanish waters or coastlines.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate November 26-27 emergency—capsize, rescue and spill-prevention efforts—not the eventual salvage outcome, formal cause investigation, liability proceedings or longer-term environmental assessment.
